name: Gecko
tagline: the runner: stick to mass, run it, hop
summary: The runner. Hold LT near any mass and it sticks, then runs along the structure: the chain of prisms guides its course, its speed climbs to 130 u/s, the camera rolls onto the surface, and a rival's rail it runs becomes yours. Let go, or press RT, and it hops off with a ×1.4 kick and three seconds of carried momentum to the next surface. Wall-running, where every prismscape is a wall.

spec.v: LT stick and run along mass · release / RT hop
to 130 u/s on a surface, 50 free
wall-running: Titanfall 2, Ghostrunner, Mario Kart World's wall ride

fantasy: It treats the prismscape as a climbing gym. A good lap never touches open space: ribbon, rival rail, cluster, hop, ribbon.
why: Wall-running converts geometry into speed and players chain it once they trust the wall (Titanfall's 2x rule, Ghostrunner 2.5M, Mario Kart World's wall-ride meta). The Urchin grinds a line at 300 on its own rail; the Gecko runs the outside of ANY mass at a gain and the fun is the hop between surfaces. Camera tilt onto the surface is the tell.

notModelled: The surface is a chain of prism centres, not a mesh: the hull runs a line through the structure at a fixed clearance. The game would use the prismscape topology (PrismscapeTopology) it already has.
Converting a rival rail is the Squirrel's steal rule applied by running; what super-shielded mass does under the Gecko is open.
